bm_curator.text: Welcome to the old Commissioner's House. Mind the cannonballs. The stairs are worse.
In 1609 the Sea Venture hit the reef in a hurricane, bound for Virginia. Everyone got ashore. The ship was less lucky.
The survivors built two little ships from Bermuda cedar, and sailed on in 1610. A few stayed, and the island has had people ever since.
And a man called Strachey wrote a letter about the storm and the island that got passed round London. Some say Shakespeare read it before he wrote The Tempest.

bm_guide.text: The Navy built the Dockyard from 1809, much of it by convicts. It sits on Ireland Island at the west end of the chain. Look at the thickness of those walls.

The Dockyard's job was to mend ships that had crossed the Atlantic and fought across it. Bermuda's reefs and narrow gaps meant enemies had to pick their way in. Bermudian pilots, however, found it easy.
